liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Saint Stephen** (3 reviews): Judged the best late-era Saint Stephen, never played as hard again; Judged the best Stephen of 1978 by the reviewer [13][15][18]
- **Let It Grow** (2 reviews): Cited as a highlight, alongside Terrapin; Seriously gritty version, cited as a highlight [11][17]
- **Terrapin Station** (2 reviews): Named among the two best songs of the show; Described as virtually flawless [8][16]
- **Passenger** (1 review, 1 other source): Closer that rocks the crowd out the doors; Listed as the encore, with a corrected track listing [4][16]
- **Big River** (1 review): Singled out as outstanding, along with Let It Grow [13]
- **Brown Eyed Women** (1 other source): Clipped at the beginning on the audience tape [3]
- **Samson And Delilah** (1 review): Played with great fire; Sunrise also beautifully done [16]
- **Sunrise** (1 other source): Might be missing a little of the beginning on the audience tape [3]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-01-11.mtx.mccabe.motb0152.110959.flac16** (recommended): matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 153 min; rated 3/5 by 4 [1]
- **gd1978-01-11.mtx.sirmick.92086.sbeok.flac16**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 20 songs; 145 min; rated 4.75/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Matrix mix is fine [17]
- **gd1978-01-11.aud.unknown.89475.sbeok.flac16**: audience recording; 20 songs; 128 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [3]. Said about its sound: Audience tape has deck stopped between songs, with harsh jump cuts but no lost music [3]
- **gd78-01-11.sbd.cotsman.13190.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 17 songs; 145 min; rated 4.43/5 by 14 [6]. Said about its sound: Soundboard sounds nice, but an audience recording exists that reviewer remembers as far better, among best 1978 audience tapes; Soundboard recording quality is decent; Reviewer wants a better copy than this soundboard [11][12][13]

## Around the show

- Reviewer first heard this Let It Grow on local radio at the time [9]
- Jerry still has laryngitis from earlier in the tour but sings gamely and compensates with blistering guitar work [12]
- Jerry's voice still creaky, which the reviewer finds emotional in some songs [15]
- Band is tight and punchy like typical 1978, but Jerry's ideas and interplay lack much magic [8]
- Shows the shift from the smooth 1977 sound to the rougher, harder-driving rock of 1978 [17]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-01-11.mtx.mccabe.motb0152.110959.flac16**: taped by Rheinhart Holwein; transferred by Transfer By: Bob Menke Mastering By: Derek McCabe Matrix By: Derek McCabe; source: Analog Audience Source: FOB Master Cassettes (MAC) Analog Soundboard Source: Master Soundboard Cassette (MSC) [1]
- **gd1978-01-11.mtx.sirmick.92086.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by SirMick; source: Matrix by Sir Mick [2]. Also: Matrix chain: master cassette to 3.75 ips reel, another reel, then hard disk, wav, and flac; Matrix combines audience and soundboard sources; missing tuning and music sections were patched in from the soundboard; Dc offset removed from both sources; small dropouts and static repaired in the audience source [2]
- **gd1978-01-11.aud.unknown.89475.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Pantagruel; source: Senn404 > unknown recorder > master cassette [3]. Also: Recorded from front of balcony by Musgrave, Bunton and Martin with two Sennheiser MKH404 mics; Chain: Teac PC10 with Dolby B onto TDK SA C90 cassettes [19]
- **gd78-01-11.sbd.cotsman.13190.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [6]
